WHITE, who is the holder of the Surrey Junior title. White first showed us his form last August by winning one of our handicaps easily and in fast time, and it was most unfortunate that an accident interrupted his training for the Public Schools' Championship this April.

Rickards, Bentley, Martin and Bidgood have been the high-lights, but Rathbone, Willis, Boddington, Jarvis, Allen and White have also played their part.

White thanked the handicapper for his generosity, in winning the "half" from 30 yards in 1 min. 55 2-5 secs—excellent running. Frank Webb "snaked" a win in the High Jump handicap; and Bill Rice gave everyone the opportunity of saying "I told you so!" by easily winning the 2 miles race.
Fear of staleness has kept White out of competition, but his Championship running was superb, and we hope to see him beating two minutes consistenty next season.

George Tyrer was leading White by about a hundred yards, the latter being fifty yards ahead of the next man. After watching the majority of runners go by, I decided to get back to the winning post, so took a short cut across the Common for home.

When the Pompey runner moved away it seemed Chas. was to have one of those days , but when Haith (T.V.H.)and later White (Woodford) caught up it seemed to act as a tonic and he stayed with them to the end, where with a typical final flourish he kept us in third place, only thirty secs. down on Pompey.
Iron rallied strongly, Mac faded slightly, George Knight got cracking, and to rub salt into the wounds, White (Woodford) and Harper (Deptford) passed Mal on the run in.
